name: 花舫赌局
Painted-Barge Casino
before: 江心泊着一条花舫，灯红酒绿，骰子声隔着水都听得见。一伙海寇刀手在舫上开赌，押的不是银子，是一摞摞空白公凭：市舶司发给出海船只的凭证，十年前从司里偷出来的。有了它，私船就能装成官准的商船。赌桌上一张公凭换一条船，今晚已经输掉了三条。

A painted barge lies at anchor mid-river, red lamps and wine, the rattle of dice carrying over the water. Pirate swordsmen run a gambling den aboard, staking not silver but stacks of blank sailing certificates, the Office's permits for seagoing ships, stolen ten years ago. With one, a smuggler can pass as a licensed merchantman. At this table a certificate buys a ship, and three ships have changed hands tonight.
after: 赌徒们跳江跑了，骰子沉了底。那摞公凭里有一张不一样：抬头写着「千里号续航」，船名、货物、日期都空着，只盖着一方小小的「市舶司主簿柯」，印泥都褪了色，是十年前就盖好的。

The gamblers dive overboard and the dice sink. One certificate in the stack is different: headed 'Qianli: Continued Voyage', ship, cargo and date left blank, stamped only with a small seal, 'Ke, Registrar, Maritime Trade Office', its ink long faded. It was stamped ten years ago.

name: 旧药局
Old Powder Magazine
before: 城墙拐角下有一座半埋在土里的砖房，从前是炮台存火药的药局，墙厚三尺，门上包铁，十年前炮台收走的东西都堆在这里。如今守着它的是炮台的兵和龙记的打手，刀手、弓手、劫骑混在一起，一个穿号衣，一个穿短打，喝的是同一坛酒。

Where the city wall turns, a brick building lies half buried: the fort's old powder magazine, walls three feet thick, door clad in iron, where everything the fort confiscated ten years ago is piled. It's guarded now by fort soldiers and Long house bruisers together, swordsmen, archers and riders mixed, uniform tunics beside short jackets, drinking from the same jar.
after: 守兵败退，铁门撬开。火药桶早空了，屋里码着一摞摞折起来的油纸灯笼，整整三百盏，干干爽爽。陈婆拄着拐赶来，打开一盏，「千」字最后一竖拖得老长。她说那是故意的：「回来的路长，字也写长一点。」

The guards fall back and the door is forced. The powder kegs are long empty; instead the room is stacked with folded oil-paper lanterns, three hundred exactly, perfectly dry. Granny Chen hurries up on her stick and opens one. The last downstroke of its Qian is drawn out long. She did that on purpose, she says. 'It's a long way home, so I wrote it long.'

name: 锔瓷摊
Rivet-Mender's Stall
before: 路口一个锔瓷匠的摊子，专拿铜钉把碎碗锔起来。摊上供着一只怪碗，是他十年间从碎瓷滩捡回几百片碎瓷，一片片锔成的，满身铜钉，像只刺猬。一伙海寇弓手听说碗上拼出了藏宝图，要连摊子一起抬走。锔瓷匠抱着碗说，碗里只有一句话。

At a crossroads a rivet-mender staples broken bowls together with copper. On display is a strange bowl he riveted over ten years from hundreds of pieces picked off Shard Beach, bristling with copper like a hedgehog. Pirate archers have heard it shows a treasure map and want to carry it off, stall and all. Hugging it, the mender says there's only one sentence in it.
after: 弓手被赶走，锔瓷匠把碗翻过来，碗底拼出庄窑的款「庄记·千里」。他说开船前一夜，他就在这路口，看见沈船主和龙家少东家吵架。沈船主说：「这笔税你先垫，船回来我还你十倍。」少东家说：「我不要十倍，我要我弟弟下船。」后来那船瓷就封了。

The archers are run off and the mender turns the bowl over: the base pieces into the Zhuang kiln's mark, 'Zhuang: Qianli'. The night before the fleet sailed, he says, he saw Shipmaster Shen arguing with the young Long heir right here. She said, 'Advance the duty and I'll repay you tenfold when the ships come home.' He said, 'I don't want tenfold. I want my brother off that ship.' After that the porcelain was sealed.

name: 戍卒铺
Shore Watch Post
before: 炮台下的海边有座哨铺，门口钉着一块木牌，写着三条规矩：「一、子时不许点灯。二、夏夜海上若见三百点光，不许数，不许划船去追。三、有人来问千里号回来没有，答『没有』，不许多说一个字。」哨铺如今被一伙海寇刀手占着，他们也照规矩办，半夜黑灯瞎火，缩在墙角不敢出声。

On the shore below the fort stands a watch post with a board of three rules nailed to its door. 'One: no lamps at midnight. Two: if on a summer night you see three hundred lights on the sea, do not count them and do not row after them. Three: if anyone asks whether the Qianli has come back, answer No, and not one word more.' Pirate swordsmen hold it now, and they keep the rules too, huddled silent in the dark at midnight.
after: 刀手被赶走。当夜海上果然亮起蓝光，一浪一闪：是海里的夜光虫，夏夜被浪一搅就发光。几年前两个新兵当成千里号的灯，划船去追，没再回来，老炮手才定了第二条。第一条是怕灯光招海寇。第三条？来问的是喝醉的吴把总，多说一句他能哭到天亮。

The swordsmen are thrown out. That night the sea does light up blue, flickering with each wave: tiny glowing creatures that shine when summer waves stir them. Years ago two recruits took it for the Qianli's lanterns, rowed after it and never returned, so the old gunner made rule two. Rule one keeps lights from drawing pirates. Rule three? The midnight asker is Captain Wu, drunk; say one word more and he weeps till dawn.

name: 说书棚
Storyteller's Booth
before: 码头边一座草棚，说书先生一块醒木，天天讲《千里号》。台下坐满了海寇弓手，他们不爱听没结局的故事，逼先生每晚换个结局：今晚满载金银回港，明晚娶了龙女，后晚打下海外三十国。先生讲得口干舌燥，结局已经编到第三百零七个了。

In a straw booth by the docks a storyteller with a clapper-block tells 'The Qianli' every day. His audience is packed with pirate archers who can't stand a story without an ending and make him change it nightly: tonight it comes home laden with gold, tomorrow it marries the Dragon King's daughter, the night after it conquers thirty kingdoms. His throat is parched, and he's up to ending number three hundred and seven.
after: 弓手们被请出了棚子。先生说这故事本来没有结局，他只讲到七号驳被拖回去就停。每年八月，有个包头巾的番商来听这一段，听完放下一枚银币就走，从不问结局，只问一句：「那船瓷，什么时候到？」

The archers are shown out. The story never had an ending, the storyteller says; he only told it as far as barge No. 7 being towed back. Every August a turbaned foreign merchant comes to hear that part, leaves a silver coin and goes, never asking the ending, only one thing: 'That porcelain. When will it arrive?'

name: 舶牌坊
Ship-Tally Workshop
before: 小巷深处一间作坊，老匠人专刻舶牌：出海的船每条一块，刻着船名、船主、编号，进出港都要验。一伙海寇刀手占着作坊，逼他给私船刻假牌。他刻是刻了，每块背后都偷偷刻一只王八。墙上还挂着一块落了灰的旧牌，十年没人来领。

Deep in an alley a workshop carves ship tallies: one wooden tag for every seagoing ship, carved with name, master and number, checked on every entry and departure. Pirate swordsmen have taken it and make the old carver cut fake tallies for smugglers. He does, but secretly carves a tortoise, the old insult, on the back of each. On the wall hangs one dusty tally nobody has collected in ten years.
after: 刀手被打跑，老匠人摘下那块旧牌吹掉灰：「千里·七」。千里号七条船的舶牌都是他刻的，六块领走了，这块一直挂着。「出海要三样：市舶司的公凭，我这块牌子，还得炮台放行。」他把牌子交给你们，「剩下两样，你们去讨。」

The swordsmen are chased out and the carver takes down the old tally and blows off the dust: 'Qianli 7'. He carved all seven of the Qianli's tallies; six were collected, and this one has hung here since. 'To sail you need three things: the Office's certificate, my tally, and the fort's leave.' He hands it over. 'The other two, go and get yourselves.'

name: 投军坪
Enlistment Green
before: 城外一片坪地上插着一面黑旗：「投海寇者，管饭，发刀。」市舶司关门十年，码头的脚夫、挑夫、扛包的没活干，一拨拨往这里来。招兵头目坐在桌后点名，刀手、弓手、劫骑都收，新来的连刀都握反了，还嚷着要当大头领。

A black flag flies over a green outside town: 'Join the pirates: meals provided, blades issued.' With the Office shut ten years, the dock porters, carriers and stevedores have no work and come here wave after wave. The recruiting chief calls names behind a table, taking swordsmen, archers and riders alike. The newest hold their blades backwards and still clamour to be captains.
after: 这一拨新兵被打散，多半扔了刀回城找活。招兵簿上记着：「脚夫十七，挑夫九，市舶司旧库丁三。」可黑旗还插着，码头上没活的人总有，过不了几天又会来一拨。等市舶司的门真开了，来的人或许会少一些。

This wave is scattered and most throw down their blades and go back to town for work. The roll reads: 'Porters 17, carriers 9, former Office store guards 3.' But the black flag still flies and there are always idle men on the docks, so in a few days another wave will come. Once the Office truly opens, perhaps fewer will.

name: 旗语楼
Signal-Flag Tower
before: 平野上一座木楼，楼顶竖着旗杆，从前炮台用旗语跟港里的船说话：红旗停船，黄旗验货，黑旗开炮。一伙海寇弓手偷了炮台的旗谱，占了旗楼，挂起乱七八糟的旗，港里的船有的停、有的跑、有的原地打转，弓手们在楼上笑得直拍栏杆。

A timber tower on the plain carries a flagpole the fort once used to talk to ships by flag: red to heave to, yellow for inspection, black for cannon fire. Pirate archers have stolen the fort's flag book and taken the tower, hoisting nonsense, so ships in the harbour stop, flee or spin in circles while the archers laugh and slap the rail.
after: 弓手被赶下楼，乱旗都降了。旗谱后面夹着十年前的值夜记：「八月十八子时，港内见千字灯三百，奉把总令挂黑旗，令其灭灯停船。灯灭。四更，灯复亮一盏，船出。」灯是灭了，船没停。

The archers are driven down and the flags lowered. Tucked in the back of the flag book is a night log from ten years ago: 'Eighteenth of the eighth month, midnight. Three hundred Qian lanterns in harbour. By the Captain's order, black flag hoisted: lights out, ships to stop. Lights out. Fourth watch: one lantern relit. Ships departed.' The lights went out. The ships didn't stop.

name: 外炮坡
Outer Battery Slope
before: 城墙外的山坡上一排土炮台，炮口对着港门。守炮的兵早不打海寇了，在坡下设了一道「出港查验」，出港的船都要停下交钱，交够了才不开炮：刀手查货，弓手站炮位，劫骑去追想溜的船。港里的船家说，这道坡比海寇还难过。

A row of earthwork batteries lines the slope outside the wall, guns on the harbour gate. The garrison stopped fighting pirates long ago and runs an 'outbound inspection' at the foot of the slope: every departing ship stops and pays, and only when it has paid enough do they hold fire. Swordsmen check cargo, archers man the guns, riders chase anyone slipping past. Boatmen say this slope is worse than the pirates.
after: 卡子拆了，炮手们灰溜溜缩回了炮位。卡房账上，除了过路钱，还有一笔进账，十年里每月一次，一次不少：「龙记，灯油钱，二十两。」旁边只注了四个字：「千字不出」。

The checkpoint is torn down and the gunners slink back. In its accounts, besides the tolls, is another income, every month for ten years without a miss: 'Long house, lamp-oil money, twenty taels.' The note beside it is four words: 'No Qian goes out.'

name: 市舶司
Maritime Trade Office
before: 港口最气派的一座衙门，门前两只石狮子，朱漆大门剥得斑斑驳驳。十年前这里番商云集，如今大门紧闭，门前被一伙海寇刀手占了，摆摊收「代办费」：要出海、要卸货，都得经他们的手。柯提举站在台阶下，看着自己的衙门，进不去。

The grandest yamen in the harbour, stone lions at the gate, its vermilion doors peeling. Ten years ago foreign merchants thronged here; now the gates are shut and pirate swordsmen have set up stalls outside charging 'handling fees': to sail or to unload, everything goes through them. Superintendent Ke stands at the foot of the steps looking up at his own yamen, unable to get in.
after: 刀手被赶走，大门十年来头一回打开，番商的金子换船坞的木料，买卖又做起来了。柯提举在大堂上摊开半张纸海图，把十二只青花盘围成一圈：盘心的线一只接一只，连上纸上的海岸，从泉州出港往东南去，一直画进一片空白，空白上写着一个「雾」字。「续航要三个保人重新画押，」他说，「庄窑主，我，还有龙家。」

The swordsmen are thrown out, the gates open for the first time in ten years, and trade resumes: foreign merchants' gold for shipyard timber. In the hall Superintendent Ke spreads his half paper chart and sets the twelve plates in a ring around it. The lines in the plates join one to the next and meet the coast on the paper: out of Quanzhou, southeast, on into a blank space marked with one character: Fog. 'A continued voyage needs the three guarantors to sign again,' he says. 'Master Zhuang, myself, and the Long house.'

name: 蕃坊驿
Foreign Quarter Inn
before: 蕃坊是番商住的街坊，街口一座大驿馆，院里有喷水的石池，屋顶是圆的。番商走了十年，驿馆被一伙码头劫骑占了，马拴在石池边饮水，骑手们躺在番商的地毯上啃甘蔗。驿馆的老掌柜会说七种番话，如今只用来干一件事：骂人。

The Foreign Quarter is where the overseas merchants lived, and at its entrance stands a large inn with a fountain basin and domed roofs. With the merchants gone ten years, dockside raiders have taken it, watering their horses at the fountain and lounging on the carpets chewing cane. The old innkeeper speaks seven foreign tongues and now uses them for one thing only: cursing.
after: 劫骑被赶出去，地毯拍了三天灰。市舶司开门的消息一传开，港外就有番船靠过来了。老掌柜说，有几条番船在沙坝外等了好几年，就等市舶司的灯一亮。「他们说，泉州是海上的大门，门一关，海就小了。」

The raiders are turned out and the carpets get three days' beating. As word spreads that the Office has opened, foreign ships begin to come in; some, says the innkeeper, have waited outside the bar for years for the Office's lamps to light. 'They say Quanzhou is the gate of the sea. Shut the gate and the sea shrinks.'
first: 驿馆里抄出劫骑囤的二十袋番米、一箱胡椒、三张垫在马鞍下的波斯毯，还有一大罐番商留下的蜜枣，已经被吃得只剩罐底。

In the inn you seize the raiders' hoard: twenty sacks of foreign rice, a chest of pepper, three Persian carpets used as saddle blankets, and a big jar of honeyed dates the merchants left, eaten down to the bottom.
pass: 每次路过，老掌柜都用七种番话问候你们一遍，再端上一壶加了豆蔻的番茶和一盘烤饼，说番商们托他招待「开门的人」。
Every time you pass, the old innkeeper greets you in all seven tongues and serves cardamom tea and flatbread. The merchants asked him, he says, to look after 'the ones who opened the door'.

name: 押契寮
Pledge Shed
before: 平野上一间草寮，寮外插着龙记钱庄的旗，一伙海寇弓手看着一个十来岁的男孩，男孩满手是泥，被逼着捏一只又一只泥碗。他是庄大炉的孙子：窑主这些年靠借龙记的钱过日子，还不上，孙子就被押在这里抵利钱。弓手们拿泥碗当酒碗，摔一只，他捏一只。

A straw shed on the plain flies a Long Bank flag. Pirate archers watch a boy of ten or so, hands caked in clay, made to shape clay bowl after clay bowl. He's Zhuang Dalu's grandson: the kiln master has lived on Long Bank loans these past years and can't repay, so the boy is held against the interest. The archers use the bowls as wine cups; for every one they smash, he makes another.
after: 弓手被打跑，孩子揣着最后一只泥碗跑回了龙窑。庄大炉拄着拐来到市舶司，在新保状上按下手印，按得很重，像要按进纸里去：「我这把老骨头作保，那船瓷，这回得出海。」

The archers are beaten off and the boy runs home to the kiln with his last clay bowl. Zhuang Dalu hobbles to the Office and presses his thumbprint on the new surety so hard he seems to push it into the paper. 'I stand surety with these old bones. This time that porcelain goes to sea.'

name: 铳头面馆
Gunner's Noodle House
before: 炮台下的小街上有一家面馆，老板是退伍的老炮手，人称秦铁口，耳朵早被炮震聋了，说话像打雷。一伙海寇刀手天天来吃面不给钱，吃完还要再来一碗。秦铁口听不见，只看口型，一律当成「再来一碗」，已经下了四十碗，刀手们撑得走不动了。

On the little street below the fort is a noodle house run by a retired gunner, Iron-Mouth Qin, deafened long ago by cannon, who talks like thunder. Pirate swordsmen come daily to eat without paying and demand another bowl. Qin reads lips and takes everything as 'another bowl'. He's served them forty, and they're too stuffed to move.
after: 刀手们是爬着出去的。秦铁口擦着灶台说，那一夜他是炮长，把总下令往港里开一炮吓住千里号。「我装了火药，没装炮子。」那一炮只响不打，船队灭了灯，又亮起一盏，就出去了。「我这耳朵就是那一炮震聋的。值。」

The swordsmen leave on hands and knees. Wiping the stove, Qin says that on that night he was gun captain, ordered to fire one shot into the harbour to scare the Qianli. 'I loaded the powder. I didn't load the ball.' All noise, no strike; the fleet put out its lights, relit one, and sailed. 'That's the shot that deafened me. Worth it.'

name: 紫菜岩
Laver Rocks
before: 炮台崖下的礁岩上长着紫菜，退潮时，采菜的女人们腰上拴着绳子，贴着湿滑的岩壁一片片刮。一伙海寇弓手占了礁岩，说紫菜归他们，刮一篮收一篮。领头的采菜女叫阿蓝，刮得最快，绳子拴得最松，她说她不怕掉下去。

Laver grows on the rocks beneath the fort's cliff. At low tide the women who gather it tie ropes round their waists and press against the slick rock, scraping it off sheet by sheet. Pirate archers have taken the rocks: a basket gathered, a basket taken. The lead gatherer, A'lan, scrapes fastest and ties her rope loosest. She says she isn't afraid of falling.
after: 弓手被赶下礁，紫菜晒上了岩顶。阿蓝的男人就是哨铺那两个划船追蓝光的新兵之一。她不怪谁，只说秦铁口每月都从饷里拿一半给她，「他说那条规矩定晚了。」她送你们一捆紫菜，又补一句：「把总也给，偷偷的，不敢让龙家知道。」

The archers are driven off and the laver spread to dry on the clifftop. A'lan's husband was one of the two recruits who rowed after the blue lights. She blames no one, but says Qin has given her half his pay every month. 'He says he made that rule too late.' She gives you a bundle of laver and adds, 'The Captain gives too, on the quiet. He daren't let the Long house know.'

name: 摸黑市
Dark Market
before: 城外的夜市十年不许点灯，龙记说「灯油钱交给炮台了，夜里不许再亮」，只准买龙记的灯笼，一盏顶十盏的价。百姓不买，夜市就摸黑做买卖：摸鱼鳞猜新鲜，捏布料猜颜色，数铜钱全凭手指头。刀手、弓手、劫骑在黑地里来回转，专抢摸错了的人。

For ten years the night market outside town has been forbidden lamps. 'The lamp-oil money's paid to the fort,' says the Long house; 'nothing lights up at night', except Long lanterns, at ten times the price. The people won't buy, so the market trades in the dark: feeling fish scales for freshness, pinching cloth to guess its colour, counting coppers by fingertip. Swordsmen, archers and riders prowl the dark, robbing anyone who fumbles.
after: 打手们被赶跑，有人摸出火石点起灯，一盏接一盏，整条夜市亮了。卖布的大嫂一看自己的布，惊叫：「我把红的当绿的卖了十年！」老人们说，那年八月十八夜里，夜市的人都跑到海边点灯送船，炮台一声令下，灯全灭了，第二天就有了不许点灯的规矩。

The bruisers are chased off. Someone feels out a flint and lights a lamp, then another, until the whole market glows. The cloth-seller looks at her bolts and shrieks: 'I've been selling the red as green for ten years!' The old folk say that on that night in the eighth month the whole market ran to the shore with lamps to see the ships off; at the fort's command every lamp went out, and the next day came the rule of no lights.

name: 讼师楼
Litigator's Loft
before: 巷子里一座小楼，住着个瘦讼师，十年里替陈婆告了炮台五十二回，告的是「强收灯笼三百盏，未付分文」。状子递了五十二回，驳回五十二回，他还在写第五十三回。炮台雇了一伙海寇刀手来砸他的楼，他躲在桌子底下，还在磨墨。

In an alley stands a little loft where a skinny litigator lives. In ten years he has sued the fort fifty-two times on Granny Chen's behalf, for 'forcible seizure of three hundred lanterns, unpaid'. Fifty-two petitions, fifty-two dismissals, and he's writing the fifty-third. The fort has hired pirate swordsmen to wreck the loft; he hides under his desk, still grinding ink.
after: 刀手们被赶下楼。讼师爬出来翻开五十二份批文，每一份末尾都是同一句：「千字禁令，非官府所颁，无从撤销。」他拍桌大笑：「官府没颁过！那是谁颁的？」他在第五十三份状子上添了个被告：龙记。

The swordsmen are thrown downstairs. The litigator crawls out and leafs through the fifty-two rulings: each ends with the same sentence: 'The Qian ban was not issued by the authorities and so cannot be revoked.' He slaps the desk and roars. 'The authorities never issued it! Then who did?' On the fifty-third petition he adds a defendant: the Long house.

name: 验货坞
Inspection Dock
before: 市舶司的验货坞是一道石砌长堤，番船进港都要靠在这里开舱验货。十年没人验货，长堤成了私货码头，一伙海寇刀手每到半夜就在这里卸私盐、私铁、私香料，灯也不点，全凭摸。白天他们睡在堤上，拿验货官的印台当枕头。

The Office's inspection dock is a long stone jetty where every foreign ship tied up to open its holds. With no inspections for ten years, it's a contraband landing: every midnight pirate swordsmen unload smuggled salt, iron and spice here without a light, by feel. By day they sleep on the jetty with the inspector's inkpad for a pillow.
after: 刀手被赶下堤，印台洗干净摆回了桌上。柯提举叫人把七号驳从封库拖来，靠上验货坞，三千件瓷一件件过秤、点数、贴新签。点到最后，缺的五箱和十二只盘都对上了数，只差龙家一个手印。

The swordsmen are thrown off and the inkpad washed and set back on its desk. Superintendent Ke has barge No. 7 towed from the bonded store to the inspection dock, and all three thousand pieces are weighed, counted and relabelled. In the end the five missing crates and the twelve plates are all accounted for. All that's lacking is the Long house's thumbprint.

name: 三百碗
Three Hundred Bowls
before: 港边一间粥铺，每年一进八月，老板娘就在门口摆开三百只粗碗，每晚盛满热粥，摆到天亮，再端给街上的乞丐。一伙海寇弓手说她「招鬼」，要她交「镇鬼钱」，不交就把碗一只只射碎。老板娘站在碗阵中间，拿勺子敲着锅沿骂，一只也不让。

By the harbour is a porridge shop. Every year when the eighth month comes, its proprietress sets three hundred coarse bowls before her door, fills them with hot porridge every night, leaves them till dawn, then gives them to the beggars. Pirate archers say she's 'calling up ghosts' and demand 'ghost-quelling money', or they'll shoot the bowls to pieces. She stands among her ranks of bowls banging the pot with her ladle and cursing, refusing to give up one.
after: 弓手被赶跑，碎了的碗只有七只。老板娘说，那年她就站在这门口，看见三百盏灯一齐灭了，港里黑得像墨；过了一会儿，船头又亮起一盏，就一盏，一直往港门外去。「那是船主的灯，我认得。」从那年起，她每年摆三百只碗：「总得有人替她们备着饭。」

The archers are driven off; only seven bowls broke. She stood in this doorway that year, she says, and saw three hundred lanterns go out at once, the harbour black as ink. After a while one lantern lit again at a bow, just one, and moved steadily out of the harbour gate. 'The shipmaster's lantern. I knew it.' Every year since, she's set out three hundred bowls. 'Someone has to keep a meal ready for them.'

name: 印房洲
Seal-Vault Islet
before: 江心小洲上有一间石屋，铁门三道，从前是市舶司存大印的印房。十年前七号驳的税没交上，按律提举要把大印押出去作保，押给了谁，柯提举至今不肯说。如今石屋由龙记最精锐的打手守着：刀手堵门，弓手守岸，劫骑在浅滩上来回踏水。

On a small islet mid-river stands a stone house behind three iron doors, once the vault of the Office's great seal. Ten years ago, when barge No. 7's duty went unpaid, the law required the Superintendent to pledge the great seal as security. To whom, Superintendent Ke still won't say. The Long house's finest guard it now: swordsmen at the door, archers on the shore, riders splashing through the shallows.
after: 三道铁门打开，大印端端正正摆在石台上，印匣上还系着当年的红绳。旁边一口箱子，装着那船瓷的税银，外加十年的利息，一文不差。箱上压着龙家少东家的字条：「税我交。船回来那天，再交。」

The three doors open. The great seal sits squarely on its stone altar, its case still tied with that year's red cord. Beside it is a chest holding exactly the duty on the porcelain plus ten years' interest, to the copper. On top lies a note in the Long heir's hand: 'I'll pay the duty. On the day the ships come home, I'll pay it.'

name: 四更楼
Fourth-Watch Tower
before: 城墙上一座更楼，更夫每夜打更：一更、二更、三更，到了四更却从来不敲，直接跳到五更。一伙海寇弓手占了更楼，嫌吵，把更鼓扔下了城墙。老更夫抱着鼓槌坐在墙垛上，说他少打了十年四更，再少一夜不碍事，可这鼓不能丢。

A drum tower stands on the city wall where the watchman beats the hours each night: first watch, second, third. The fourth he never beats; he skips straight to the fifth. Pirate archers have taken the tower and, sick of the noise, thrown his drum off the wall. The old watchman sits on the battlements hugging his sticks. He's skipped the fourth watch ten years, he says, and one more night won't hurt, but that drum mustn't be lost.
after: 弓手被赶下城，鼓从墙根捡了回来。老更夫翻开更簿，十年前八月十八那页，四更底下写着：「千里号出港，炮台放空炮一声。」那以后把总说四更「不吉利」，不许再打。今夜他犹豫了一下，轻轻敲了一记四更。

The archers are driven off and the drum fetched from the wall's foot. In the watch book, on the page for that night ten years ago, under the fourth watch: 'The Qianli departs. The fort fires one blank.' Afterwards the Captain declared the fourth watch 'unlucky' and forbade it. Tonight, after a moment's hesitation, the old man beats the fourth watch once, very softly.

name: 抄榜墙
Notice Wall
before: 市舶司门外的照壁上新贴了一张大榜：「千里号七号驳续航，招水手、舵工、伙夫若干。」墨迹未干，一伙海寇弓手就拿箭把榜射成了筛子，又贴上自己的一张：「谁敢上船，先问龙爷。」想报名的水手们站在远处探头探脑，不敢走近。

A big notice has just gone up on the screen wall outside the Office: 'Qianli barge No. 7, continued voyage. Hiring sailors, helmsmen, cooks.' The ink isn't dry before pirate archers have shot it full of holes and pasted up their own: 'Anyone who dares board, ask Master Long first.' Would-be sailors stand at a distance craning their necks, not daring to come closer.
after: 弓手被赶跑，大榜重新贴上，水手们排起长队，一个白胡子老舵工排在第一。榜底下不知谁用炭写了一行小字：「瓷有了，凭有了，牌有了。龙王不点头，船出不了一号泊。」

The archers are driven off, the notice goes back up, and the sailors form a long queue, a white-bearded old helmsman at its head. Beneath the notice someone has added in charcoal: 'Porcelain, certificate, tally: all here. If the Dragon King doesn't nod, no ship leaves Berth One.'

name: 海蚀洞
Sea-Cut Cave
before: 炮台下的海崖上开着一个大洞，涨潮时洞口没在水里，只有退潮才露出来。洞边立着一根孤零零的石柱，像一根插在海里的手指。一伙码头劫骑专趁退潮骑马进洞藏私货，等潮一涨，洞口自己封上，谁也找不着。今天潮刚退，马蹄声正在洞里回响。

In the sea cliff below the fort opens a great cave whose mouth is drowned at high tide and shows only at the ebb. Beside it stands a lone pillar of rock like a finger stuck in the sea. Dockside raiders ride in at every low tide to stash contraband, and when the tide rises the mouth seals itself. The tide has just gone out, and hoofbeats echo inside.
after: 劫骑被堵在洞里收拾了。秦铁口说这洞是浪掏出来的：浪专打崖脚，先打出凹槽，再掏成洞，哪天打穿成了石拱，拱顶一塌，外头那截就成了旁边那样的孤柱。洞底一条烂舢板里有封油纸裹的信：「请放行。所欠之税，沈渡一人担。」那夜，这信没送到炮台。

The raiders are cornered inside and dealt with. Qin says the waves dug this cave: they pound the cliff's foot, cut a notch, scoop it into a cave; one day it breaks through into an arch, the arch roof falls, and the outer part is left standing like that pillar. At the back lies a rotted skiff holding an oilpaper-wrapped letter: 'Please let us pass. The duty owed, Shen Du alone will answer for.' That night it never reached the fort.

name: 银车道
Silver-Cart Road
before: 一辆蒙着油布的马车在路上走，车轮压得很深，前后一队码头劫骑护着。每月初一它都走这条路，从龙记钱庄到炮台，路边的人都知道车上是什么：龙记给炮台的「灯油钱」。这个月的车刚上路，劫骑们挥着鞭子，把挡路的鸭群赶得满天飞。

A wagon under an oilcloth rolls along the road, wheels biting deep, a troop of dockside raiders riding escort. On the first of every month it travels from the Long Bank to the fort, and everyone along the way knows what it carries: the Long house's 'lamp-oil money'. This month's wagon has just set out, and the riders crack their whips, sending a flock of ducks flapping across the sky.
after: 劫骑被打散，车上果然是二十两银子，红纸封着，写「灯油」。老车夫说他赶这趟车十年，每回龙爷都亲自看着装车。有一回龙爷喝多了，摸着银子说：「这钱不是买他们不放船，是买他们别放错了船。」老车夫到今天也没想明白。

The riders scatter and, sure enough, the wagon holds twenty taels sealed in red paper marked 'Lamp oil'. The old carter has driven this run ten years, and every time Master Long came to watch it loaded. Once, drunk, he patted the silver and said, 'This isn't paying them not to let ships out. It's paying them not to let the wrong ship out.' The carter still hasn't worked that out.

name: 千灯巷
Thousand-Lantern Lane
before: 陈记灯笼背后有一条小巷，住着三十几户人家，十年前家家都有人给千里号做过活：缝帆的、装货的、做饭的。陈婆把药局里找回来的灯笼分给各家，巷里挂上一盏，一伙海寇弓手就在巷口射下一盏；射下一盏，巷里又挂出一盏。掉在地上的灯笼烧起来，火光把巷子照得通红。

Behind Chen's Lanterns runs a lane of thirty-odd households, every one with someone who worked for the Qianli ten years ago: sewing sails, loading cargo, cooking. Granny Chen hands out the lanterns recovered from the magazine. Each time one is hung, pirate archers at the lane's mouth shoot it down, and each time one falls, another is hung. The fallen lanterns burn, and the blaze turns the lane red.
after: 弓手被赶出巷口，巷子里挂满了「千」字灯笼，一家不少。炮台上的兵远远看着，没人开炮。陈婆点着最后一盏，挂在自家门口：「灯有了，人也有了。现在就差炮台点头，还有龙家那个泊位。」

The archers are driven out and the lane hangs full of Qian lanterns, not one household missing. The soldiers on the fort watch from afar and no one fires. Granny Chen lights the last lantern and hangs it at her own door. 'We have the lanterns and the people. All that's left is the fort's nod, and the Long house's berth.'

name: 乳香栈
Frankincense Lodge
before: 城外一座番商的货栈，门口飘着乳香的烟。栈主是个包头巾的老番商，叫哈桑，胡子染成了红色，十年来不跟泉州任何人做买卖，还雇了一伙海寇弓手守门，谁来谈生意都被射回去。他每天只做一件事：坐在门口，望着港口的方向。

Outside town stands a foreign merchant's warehouse, frankincense smoke drifting from its door. Its master is an old turbaned trader named Hassan, beard dyed red. For ten years he has traded with no one in Quanzhou and has hired pirate archers to shoot back anyone who comes to talk business. He does one thing each day: sit at his door and look toward the harbour.
after: 弓手被打退，哈桑摸着红胡子打量你们，说佩服能打进来的人，愿意开栈换货。他拿出十年前的契约：庄窑瓷三千件，卖往三佛齐，「货到之日，价加一成，不论几年」。「我等那船瓷，也等那个说话算数的女船主。去请龙家按手印吧，只差它了。」

The archers are driven back and Hassan looks you over, stroking his red beard. He respects anyone who can fight their way in and will open his stores to trade. He shows a contract from ten years ago: three thousand pieces of Zhuang porcelain for Srivijaya, 'price raised a tenth on delivery, however many years it takes'. 'I'm waiting for that porcelain, and for the woman shipmaster who kept her word. Go and get the Long house's thumbprint. It's all that's missing.'

name: 龙记货栈
Long House Godowns
before: 港后一大片货栈，几十间库房连成一条街，门楣上都挂着金色的「龙」字。泉州的商人不论卖什么，都得先把货存进这里，交了栈钱才能卖。守栈的刀手、弓手、劫骑上百人，门口的秤砣声跟骂声一样响。一个卖荔枝的小贩没交栈钱，荔枝在门口烂成了一摊酒。

Behind the harbour sprawl the godowns, dozens of storehouses joined into a street, every lintel hung with a gilded Long, dragon. Whatever a Quanzhou merchant sells must first be stored here, and only once storage is paid may it be sold. The guards, swordsmen, archers and riders, number over a hundred, and at the gates the clank of steelyard weights is as loud as the cursing. A lychee seller who didn't pay has watched his fruit rot at the door into a puddle of wine.
after: 守栈的打手被打散，商人们涌进去搬自己的货。栈簿第一页列着泉州港所有的泊位，一号泊那一栏，十年来年年同一行：「千里号，泊费，龙记自付。」自己的钱付进自己的栈，一文没少记。

The guards are scattered and merchants pour in to haul out their goods. The ledger's first page lists every berth in Quanzhou. Against Berth One, every year for ten years, the same line: 'Qianli. Berth fee. Paid by the Long house.' His own money into his own godown, and not one copper missed from the books.

name: 鸽楼
Pigeon Loft
before: 城墙边一座鸽楼，养着几十只信鸽，是吴把总的私产。他每天写一张纸条绑在鸽腿上，放往龙记。一队码头劫骑守在楼下，谁靠近就赶。鸽子吃得好，飞得懒，有一只胖得飞不上墙头，每天在楼下走着去送信。

By the city wall stands a loft of homing pigeons, Captain Wu's private property. Each day he ties a slip to a pigeon's leg and sends it to the Long house. Dockside raiders guard the loft and chase off anyone who comes near. The pigeons eat well and fly lazily; one is so fat it can't clear the wall and delivers its messages on foot.
after: 劫骑被赶跑，那只胖鸽子正好走回来，腿上绑着龙记的回条：「开拓队带灯否？带，则不拦。」你们拿去给吴把总看，他看了半天，把纸条揉成一团：「龙爷十年里头一回这么回话。」

The raiders are driven off just as the fat pigeon waddles back, a Long house reply tied to its leg: 'Does the pioneer party carry the lanterns? If so, don't stop them.' You show it to Captain Wu. He stares a long while, then crumples it. 'First time in ten years Master Long has answered like that.'

name: 镇海炮台
Sea-Guard Battery
before: 炮台最高的一层，十二门大炮排成一排，炮口对着港门。守炮顶的不全是炮台的兵，还有一队龙记派来「帮着看炮」的码头劫骑。吴把总说他已经不拦了，可劫骑们不认他的话，只认龙记的令牌，把炮口又往下压了压，对准了千灯巷那片红光。

The fort's highest tier: twelve great guns in a row, muzzles on the harbour gate. Not all who man it are soldiers: a troop of dockside raiders is here too, sent by the Long house to 'help watch the guns'. Captain Wu says he's stopped blocking anyone, but the raiders answer only to the Long house's token, and they crank the muzzles lower, aiming at the red glow of Thousand-Lantern Lane.
after: 劫骑被赶下炮台。吴把总把一张发黄的纸压在炮身上，是十年前他写给龙记的回执：「千字之船，炮台不放，凭龙记一言而解。」他说当年贪那二十两，后来是不敢收手。「禁令是我立的，可钥匙在龙爷手里。」

The raiders are driven off. Captain Wu lays a yellowed paper on a gun barrel: his receipt to the Long house from ten years ago. 'Ships bearing Qian: the fort will not release them, until the Long house says the word.' He was greedy for the twenty taels then, he says, and afterwards dared not stop. 'I set the ban. But the key is in Master Long's hand.'

name: 龙门坊
Dragon Gate Arch
before: 进龙家地界要过一座石牌坊，坊额刻着「龙门」，坊下蹲着一条石龙。守坊的海寇弓手立了规矩：过坊的人要摸一下石龙的脑袋，说一句「龙爷发财」，不够响就重说。石龙脑袋被摸得锃亮，一个结巴挑夫在坊下说了一个时辰，还没说完一句。

To enter the Long house's ground you pass a stone arch carved 'Dragon Gate', a stone dragon crouched beneath. The pirate archers guarding it have a rule: everyone pats the dragon's head and says 'Good fortune to Master Long', and if it isn't loud enough, says it again. The head is polished to a shine. A stammering porter has been at it for two hours and still hasn't got one sentence out.
after: 弓手们被赶跑，结巴挑夫一口气骂完一整句，一个字没卡。坊下摆茶摊的老头说，龙爷十年前还是个只有一条货船的少东家，十年里吃下了泉州大半的码头。「什么都能买，什么都能卖，就是一号泊，谁出多少钱他都不卖。」

The archers are run off and the stammering porter curses them out in one whole sentence without a stumble. The old man at the tea stall under the arch says that ten years ago Master Long was a young heir with one cargo ship; in ten years he's swallowed most of Quanzhou's docks. 'Everything's for sale with him. Except Berth One. Whatever anyone offers, he won't sell it.'

name: 斗蟋场
Cricket Pit
before: 一座大院里摆满瓦罐，罐里斗着蟋蟀，四面围着赌客。场子是龙记开的，海寇弓手看场子，谁赢了钱想走，弓手就拦着让他接着押。墙上挂着一块红牌，写着龙爷每年八月十八必押的一注：「千里号今年回港。」一赔一百。

A big courtyard is crowded with clay pots of fighting crickets, gamblers packed round them. The pit is the Long house's, kept by pirate archers who stop any winner from leaving and make him keep betting. On the wall hangs a red board with the wager Master Long places every year on the eighteenth of the eighth month: 'The Qianli comes home this year.' A hundred to one.
after: 弓手被赶出去，赌客们抱着罐子散了。老场主翻出赌账：这一注龙爷押了十年，年年输，年年照赔，一次没赖过。今年的注上个月就押下了，比哪年都大。「输了十年还在押，」老场主说，「你说他是信，还是不信？」

The archers are thrown out and the gamblers scatter clutching their pots. The old pit master shows the betting book: Master Long has placed this wager for ten years, lost every year, paid every year, never once welshed. This year's went down last month, bigger than ever. 'Ten years losing and still betting,' says the old man. 'Tell me: does he believe, or doesn't he?'

name: 帆布行
Sailcloth Hall
before: 长长的作坊里，女工们坐成两排缝帆，篾片撑开的硬帆一面面靠在墙上。一队码头劫骑说龙记的船要换帆，把作坊里的布都收走了，女工们没布可缝，只好缝劫骑的马鞍套。作坊后面有一间锁着的库房，劫骑想撬，老帆匠拿针扎他们的手。

In a long workshop women sit in two rows sewing sails, stiff battened sails propped along the walls. Dockside raiders, claiming the Long house ships need new sails, have taken all the cloth, so the women are stitching the raiders' saddle covers. Behind the workshop is a locked storeroom; when the raiders try to force it, the old sailmaker jabs their hands with her needle.
after: 劫骑被赶跑，布匹扛了回来。老帆匠打开库房，里面挂着一整套硬帆，篾骨崭新，帆上画着「千」。龙家每三年订一套，旧的拆了换新的，十年换了三套，没一套上过船。「龙爷说，帆旧了，船回来没得用。」

The raiders are driven off and the cloth carried back. The old sailmaker unlocks the storeroom: inside hangs a full set of battened sails, ribs new, Qian painted on the canvas. The Long house orders a set every three years and swaps out the old: three sets in ten years, not one ever aboard a ship. 'Master Long says if the sails get old, the ships will have nothing to use when they come home.'

name: 炮台夜话
Night Talk at the Fort
before: 夜里，炮台下的小院摆了一张桌子，秦铁口、吴把总、陈婆、讼师和老更夫围着一壶冷茶，谁也不先开口。院门外，龙记派来盯着把总的一伙海寇刀手来回踱步，听见里面说一个「千」字就要冲进来。陈婆把一盏没点的灯笼放在桌子正中。

At night a table is set in the little yard below the fort. Iron-Mouth Qin, Captain Wu, Granny Chen, the litigator and the old watchman sit round a pot of cold tea, and nobody wants to speak first. Outside the gate, pirate swordsmen sent by the Long house to watch the Captain pace up and down, ready to burst in at the first Qian. Granny Chen sets an unlit lantern in the very centre of the table.
after: 门外的刀手被赶走了。吴把总先开口：从今夜起，炮台不拦挂「千」字灯笼的船。秦铁口吼着说，再装一回火药，还不装炮子，给船送行。陈婆点亮了灯：「她用一盏灯出的港，我们用三百盏送她的船再出去。」讼师揣好状子：「被告龙记，就在一号泊开庭。」

The swordsmen at the gate are driven off. Captain Wu speaks first: from tonight the fort won't stop any ship with Qian lanterns. Qin bellows that he'll load powder once more, and once more no ball: a send-off. Granny Chen lights the lantern. 'She left with one lantern. We'll send her ship out again with three hundred.' The litigator pockets his petition. 'Defendant: the Long house. Court sits at Berth One.'

name: 浮木澳
Driftwood Cove
before: 每次刮过大风，这片海湾都会漂来一层木头：断桅、船板、整根原木。一队码头劫骑占着海滩，说漂上岸的木头都归龙记。一个扎短辫的姑娘不管不顾，扛起一根黑沉沉的木头就跑，跑不快，被劫骑追着绕礁石转圈，嘴里还喊：「这根是铁力木，你们不识货！」

After every big blow a layer of timber washes into this cove: broken masts, planks, whole logs. Dockside raiders hold the beach, saying every stick that lands belongs to the Long house. A girl with a short braid ignores them, shoulders a heavy dark log and runs, too slowly, so the raiders chase her round and round the rocks while she yells, 'This one's ironwood, you don't know what you're looking at!'
after: 劫骑被赶下海滩，姑娘把木头往地上一戳，喘着气说她叫阿樯，是船匠龚墨斗的徒弟。师父照着千里号的船样造了十年船，还差几样东西。「铁力木做舵杆，十年都不烂。」她拍拍木头，「师父说，这条船造好了，就能去追千里号。」

The raiders are driven off. The girl plants the log upright and, breathing hard, says she's A'qiang, apprentice to the shipwright Gong Modou. Her master has spent ten years building a ship to the Qianli's model and is short only a few things. 'Ironwood for the rudder post. It won't rot in ten years.' She pats the log. 'Master says once this ship is done, it can go after the Qianli.'

name: 义仓
Charity Granary
before: 港后的高地上有一座石砌义仓，门口石碑刻着：「千里号三百家，岁给米三石，龙四海立。」每年开仓放米给千里号的家眷。可这两年管仓的管事监守自盗，雇了一队码头劫骑锁了仓门，把米倒卖给米行，家眷们来领米，只领回一顿鞭子。

On high ground behind the harbour stands a stone charity granary. Its stele reads: 'For the three hundred households of the Qianli, three piculs of rice a year. Erected by Long Sihai.' Every year it opened to the families of the Qianli's crews. But these two years the steward has been robbing his own charge: he's hired dockside raiders to lock the gates and sells the rice on, and families who come for it go home with a whipping.
after: 管事被捆了送去龙记，仓门重开。碑上的「龙四海」，就是海龙王的本名。排队领米的老太太们说，龙爷嘴硬心软，十年没说过千里号一句好话，米却一年没少过，只是从不许人说是他给的。

The steward is trussed up and sent to the Long house, and the granary opens again. The 'Long Sihai' on the stele is the Dragon King's real name. The old women in the queue say Master Long has a hard mouth and a soft heart: ten years without a good word for the Qianli, yet never a year short of rice. He just never lets anyone say it came from him.
first: 仓里抄出管事藏的四十石陈米、两窖番薯干，还有一本倒卖账，最后一笔写着：「卖米一百石，得银三十两，龙爷若问，就说鼠吃了。」

You find what the steward hid: forty piculs of old rice, two cellars of dried sweet potato, and his ledger of sales, whose last entry reads: 'Sold 100 piculs for 30 taels. If Master Long asks, say rats ate it.'
pass: 每次路过，领米的老太太们都给你们包一串咸肉粽子，还要叮嘱一句：「替我们看看海上，有没有船回来。」
Every time you pass, the old women wrap you a string of salt-pork rice dumplings, with the same request each time: 'Keep an eye on the sea for us. See if any ships are coming home.'

name: 红头寨
Red-Headband Hold
before: 平野上一座新扎的寨子，寨里的海寇都扎红头巾，弓手尤其多。头领红头三是从南边海上来的，扬言要接海龙王的码头：「龙王老了，守着个空泊位发呆，泉州该换人了。」他给龙记下过三回战书，三回都原样退了回来，连封口都没拆。

A new stockade stands on the plain, its pirates all in red headbands, archers especially. Their chief, Red-Head San, came up from the southern seas boasting he'll take over the Dragon King's docks: 'The Dragon King's gone soft, mooning over an empty berth. Quanzhou needs new blood.' He's sent the Long house three declarations of war, and all three came back unopened.
after: 红头寨被打散，红头三逃回了海上。寨里搜出他的探子报：「龙四海每夜子时到一号泊，坐一个时辰，不带人，不点灯。」探子添了一句：「此人可劫。」红头三在旁批了两个字：「不劫。」大概连海寇也觉得，这时候劫他不像话。

The hold is broken and Red-Head San flees back to sea. In the stockade is his spy's report: 'Long Sihai goes to Berth One every midnight and sits two hours, no escort, no lamp.' The spy added: 'Could be snatched.' Beside it Red-Head San wrote one word: 'Don't.' It seems even a pirate felt robbing him then wouldn't be decent.

name: 桐油坡
Tung-Oil Slope
before: 山坡上一片油桐树，树下一座榨油的小作坊，桐子榨出的桐油是造船补缝的命根子。一队码头劫骑把作坊包了，榨出来的油全运去龙记船厂，一滴也不卖给别人。阿樯说师父的船只差最后几舱没艌好，要的就是这里的油。

Tung trees cover the hillside above a small oil press. Tung oil is the lifeblood of shipbuilding, for caulking seams. Dockside raiders have taken over the press and send every drop to the Long shipyard, selling none to anyone else. A'qiang says her master's ship is only missing the caulking in its last few holds, and this is the oil it needs.
after: 劫骑被赶走，油坊老板娘装了三桶桐油给你们。阿樯一边捆桶一边说：桐油掺上石灰和捣碎的麻丝，捶成油灰塞进船板缝里，干了比石头还硬，海水一滴也渗不进。「千里号的缝，当年就是这么一道道艌出来的。」

The raiders are driven off and the mistress of the press fills three barrels for you. Tying them down, A'qiang explains: mix tung oil with lime and pounded hemp, beat it into putty, ram it into the seams. Dry, it's harder than stone and not a drop of seawater gets through. 'That's how every seam on the Qianli was caulked.'
